To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) URL Tree is a novel and efficient algorithm that is suitable for content extraction in a streaming setting, (2) the algorithm outperforms several state-of-the-art content extraction algorithms in a streaming setting on a semi-automatically labeled dataset, and (3) the presented pipeline is an efficient and language-independent content extraction infrastructure.

(i) URL Tree is an efficient unsupervised and language-independent algorithm for content extraction from streams; (ii) the performance of URL tree is already competitive after processing only 10 to a few 100 documents from the same domain; and (iii) the proposed infrastructure for content extraction from HTML document streams is a useful tool for the analysis of streams of Web documents.

(1) URL tree is an efficient, unsupervised, language-independent content extraction approach that can outperform state of the art content extraction systems, and (2) the proposed infrastructure is capable of processing streams of Web documents at a rate of 1.5 million documents per hour.
